repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/2.body:
## Question

Which exact remaining gates connect the Provingkit source-stage candidate established by [Adopt the Agent Plugins v1 stack](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/pull/39) to one immutable Provingkit release?

Bind the Task Witness Linux and macOS native-host receipts, publication-grade product-attested review and issuer, detached manifest, `production_eligible` promotion, marketplace inclusion, final validation, source merge, tags, release assets, and release receipts. Distinguish existing evidence, missing evidence, sequencing, and independent authority.

## Post-cutover thread transitions

Resume this audit after [Retire Provingkit source and discovery routes from nisavid/agents](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/99) closes only in fresh post-cutover context. The assigned thread must invoke `handoff` before continuing, then restart or transfer the work to one thread dedicated to this issue. Follow [the coordinator's thread contract](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/41#thread-coordination). Suggested skills: `wayfinder`, `research`, and `domain-modeling`.

The receiving thread must revalidate current Provingkit `main`, the complete release graph, existing audit checkpoints, [Support authenticated HTTPS in the Versionkeeping publication executor](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/4), and any concurrent release or source-security threads before changing the durable answer.

After resolving this issue, do not continue directly into [Choose the production evidence producer and issuer boundary](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/8). Invoke `handoff` again and create one fresh HITL thread for that decision only if it is open, unassigned, and unblocked. Do not dispatch the release contract or publication tasks while their other native blockers remain open.

## Producer/issuer reachability checkpoint (2026-08-25)

The current candidate cannot yet produce the publication-grade Rolecasting/Tricritical evidence required by Task Witness promotion.

The Rolecasting and Tricritical Task Witness provider declarations have no registered production producers or issuers. Existing validators can consume checked-in fixtures, and the source-stage Task Witness entrypoint can validate candidate source, but no live chain can presently:

1. create product-attested Rolecasting execution evidence;
2. create the required independent Tricritical review/adjudication/loop evidence for the unchanged candidate; and
3. authenticate that evidence for the detached release manifest and final promotion.

This is a live reachability defect, not a reason to weaken Task Witness's evidence or authority semantics. It also blocks Mergecraft's required-review success path transitively; fixture success cannot substitute for a registered producer/issuer chain.

Before v1 qualification, nisavid/provingkit#2 must therefore implement and Daybreak-review the production producer and issuer boundaries, register them in the exact candidate, exercise their positive and fail-closed paths, and bind the resulting evidence into the two-host promotion chain. Until then, Task Witness remains source-stage-only and `production_eligible` remains false.

No installation, publication, signing, host adoption, or release eligibility is asserted by this checkpoint.

repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/3.title: Define the Provingkit release contract
repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/3.body:
## Question

What exact release-unit, compatibility, source-freshness, and evidence contract should govern the seven-member first Provingkit release comprising Rolecasting, Tricritical, Versionkeeping, Mergecraft, Artifact Customs, Task Witness, and Tidesmith?

Settle individual plugin versioning, the Provingkit manifest, Task Witness's special code-package route, marketplace projections, signing and digest identity, receipts, compatibility, update, revocation, reinstall, and rollback semantics. Use **Agent Plugins Specification v1.0.0** only for the external package-format contract; it is not the suite or release name.

Incorporate the complete source-skill disposition ledger and require its final upstream refresh before candidate qualification and promotion. Define which downstream evidence becomes stale when that reconciliation changes candidate bytes, and forbid release while any source contribution is undisposed or any required regenerated evidence is missing.

The first release is cohesive and self-contained. Provingkit owns every Mergecraft capability it requires at runtime, including authoring, feedback classification and placement, and both inline and top-level response actuators with source correlation, source-specific idempotency, exact-write verification, ambiguity handling, and receipts. Agentworks Discussion Comment transport remains independent equipment; it is not a Provingkit manifest member, runtime capability provider, evidence issuer, or release prerequisite. A later promotion or migration requires independent use, conformance evidence, released identities, and an explicit migration decision.

Content-lock the immutable source and behavior-evaluation evidence produced by [the portable GitHub Markdown contract implementation](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/9) and [Mergecraft feedback response routing](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/10), including the seven-field opaque-body writer boundary, the Provingkit-owned inline and top-level response actuators, exact source-to-result correlation, source-specific idempotency, exact-write reread verification, ambiguity handling, receipts, and supported-route qualification.

## Fresh synthesis boundary

Do not take this issue as a continuation of whichever prerequisite closes last. A thread carrying substantive work from any native blocker must invoke `handoff`, create a fresh HITL synthesis thread after every blocker is closed and this issue is unassigned, and stop. Follow [the coordinator's thread contract](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/41#thread-coordination). Suggested skills: `wayfinder`, `grilling`, `domain-modeling`, and the release-security skills selected by the accepted inputs.

The receiving thread must load each durable resolution and immutable evidence pointer, confirm that no concurrent thread is still changing a contract input, and coordinate with any active [Define Base Loadout and two-host binding composition](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/46) thread on the release-manifest and Resolved-Loadout seam without absorbing that issue's ownership.

After resolving this issue and updating the graph, stop and invoke `handoff` to a fresh downstream coordinator. It must repaginate the native graph, share the accepted contract revision with every receiving thread, and dispatch only independently unblocked and unassigned work. First-release publication remains a separate fresh thread under [Integrate release-ops and publish the first signed Provingkit release](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/36).

repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/4.title: Support authenticated HTTPS in the Versionkeeping publication executor
repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/4.body:
## Summary

The Versionkeeping publication planner accepts HTTPS push endpoints, but the executor's closed Git configuration clears every credential helper and sets noninteractive prompting. On a normal macOS checkout whose authenticated GitHub access comes from the system credential helper, planning succeeds while the guarded push cannot authenticate.

Observed while publishing [PR nisavid/agents#39](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/pull/39):

- `plan_git_publication.py` returned a fast-forward `ready` plan with one outgoing commit, an exact existing-target lease, and no target-only commits.
- `execute_git_publication.py` returned `POST_PUSH_STATE_UNKNOWN` with `PUSH_FAILED`.
- Three independent rereads confirmed that the remote ref remained at the exact pre-push SHA, so no remote mutation occurred.
- The checkout uses an HTTPS origin and the system `osxkeychain` helper. The executor installs a higher-precedence empty `credential.helper`, `GIT_ASKPASS=false`, and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.
- SSH is not an automatic fallback: the current host-key trust and key-authentication state may be intentionally absent.

## Desired behavior

Provide an authenticated HTTPS publication route that preserves Versionkeeping's current safety properties:

- immutable source SHA and one exact branch-update refspec;
- exact existing/absent target lease;
- captured endpoint fingerprint and configuration digest;
- noninteractive operation with no credential bytes in arguments, output, plans, receipts, or repository configuration;
- no ambient executable Git configuration;
- one actuation attempt followed by exact remote verification;
- fail-closed behavior for unsupported credential providers.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Define the trusted credential-provider boundary for authenticated HTTPS without reopening arbitrary command-valued helpers.
- [ ] Add macOS credential-provider coverage and a provider-unavailable negative path.
- [ ] Prove plans and receipts remain credential-free.
- [ ] Preserve the existing SSH and local-endpoint contracts.
- [ ] Run an independent Daybreak Blue review of the authentication and secret-handling design before implementation is accepted.

## Independent-review handoff

Begin or resume this issue in a fresh evidence-reconciliation and independent Daybreak review thread that did not implement the candidate under review. If the current thread carries that implementation context, invoke `handoff` before review. Follow [the coordinator's thread contract](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/41#thread-coordination). Suggested skills: `codex-security:security-diff-scan`, `codex-security:verify-fix`, `checkpointing-and-publishing-git-work`, and `publishing-reviewable-prs`.

If review requires remediation, publish the exact findings and reviewed revision, invoke `handoff`, and move changes to a separate fresh implementation thread. Any changed candidate then returns through another handoff to a different fresh Daybreak thread for exact-revision re-review.

Every receiving thread must coordinate its revision, evidence inputs, and conclusions with [Audit the Provingkit promotion and release chain](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/2) and concurrent source-security work. No handoff transfers credentials, publication authority, or release authority.

repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/5.body:
## Context

Issue nisavid/agents#49's source-lineage successor checks in evidence and source-stage validation without a Daybreak Blue security review. The current candidate is `1f8270c7451e75b772971dea029332eeacefe29e`; rebind to the exact merged successor before review.

## Scope

- Run an independent Daybreak Blue security diff review of the exact merged source-lineage change.
- Assess source authority, revision, content/tree digest, license, and contribution mappings for provenance or substitution gaps.
- Assess installed-host evidence for secret, username, hostname, machine-local path, and environment leakage.
- Review descriptor binding, lock and cleanup precedence, transaction recovery, refresh capture, and repository/path-swap defenses for TOCTOU or fail-open behavior.
- Decide and implement a private manager-state digest or controller attestation that spans both host-capture passes before any workflow claims stable manager-registry state.
- Consolidate the duplicated directory and non-directory no-replace move state machines behind binding-specific callbacks while preserving observable recovery and failure behavior.
- Replace deadline tests that assert private helper call counts with public-command timeout coverage, retaining only narrowly necessary propagation checks.
- Confirm diagnostics remain stable and do not surface private canaries or paths.

## Acceptance

- Record validated findings with severity, evidence, affected paths, and exact candidate identity; explicitly record a clean result if none are found.
- Exercise both directory and non-directory recovery paths through public operations after the shared-state-machine refactor.
- Prove manager-state stability is either bound to both route-capture passes or explicitly remains unasserted in public artifacts and diagnostics.
- Track remediation in separately reviewable pull requests and revalidate each fix with Daybreak Blue.
- Do not infer release eligibility, installation, promotion, host freshness, or final lineage dispositions from this review.

## Independent-review thread boundary

Begin the exact-candidate security pass in a fresh Daybreak thread independent of the implementation under review. If the pass finds changes to make, publish the findings and reviewed revision, invoke `handoff`, and move remediation to a separate fresh implementation thread. After the candidate changes, invoke `handoff` again to a different fresh Daybreak thread for exact-revision re-review. Follow [the coordinator's thread contract](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/41#thread-coordination). Suggested skills: `codex-security:security-diff-scan`, `codex-security:fix-finding`, `codex-security:verify-fix`, and `checkpointing-and-publishing-git-work`.

Before each review or mutation, coordinate candidate identity, evidence inputs, path ownership, and landing order with [security(source-skill-disposition): review and bind disposition evidence](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/6). Shared source-stage or validator inputs may have one active owner at a time; a changed shared input makes the sibling review and its handoff stale.

repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/6.title: security(source-skill-disposition): review and bind disposition evidence
repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/6.body:
## Context

Issue nisavid/agents#50 checked in a read-only source-skill disposition ledger and release-refresh contract. Subsequent reconciliation showed that several recorded decisions and validator assumptions no longer match the intended first-release topology: Tricritical must become the sole general code-review entry point, managed upstream skills must remain immutable, and source comparison must preserve useful behavior rather than reproduce documents or clauses.

This issue owns the Daybreak-reviewed security boundary that connects the corrected source evidence to the hardened reconciliation and public-release gates. Issue nisavid/provingkit#5 retains manager-state and TOCTOU hardening. Issue nisavid/provingkit#3 retains final source refresh and qualification. Issue nisavid/agents#51 retains install-before-remove convergence and host retirement.

## Scope

- Review the exact source-disposition revision and its security-sensitive integration with Daybreak.
- Record behavior-level comparisons, attribution, and ablation outcomes for the general-review baselines that feed Tricritical, including Thermos, Matt Pocock's `code-review`, Keystone's `change-review`, superseded Superpowers review routes, and any other accepted first-release candidates.
- Classify each material behavior as migrated to one named plugin owner, deliberately dropped with evidence and rationale, or retained with an existing external specialist owner.
- Keep managed or plugin-provided upstream sources immutable. A personally owned maintained derivative must bind its exact upstream revision and license.
- Do not require a rule-by-rule, clause-by-clause, phrase-level, or document-preserving map. The evidence must be detailed enough to explain the behavioral decision and reproduce the relevant comparison without rewarding duplicate wording.
- Review the lineage, disposition, and refresh validators and artifacts for provenance, privacy, path-substitution, stale-evidence, and misleading-completeness risks.
- Design and implement the hardened receipt contract that binds the corrected source manifest, behavior decisions, refresh contract, candidate identities, inventory/tree evidence, and source-reconciliation result.
- Integrate that receipt with `validate_public_release.py` and the source-stage support paths while preserving `release_eligibility: not-asserted` until every owner gate passes.
- Coordinate with nisavid/provingkit#5 without absorbing manager-state or TOCTOU scope.

## Out of scope

- Installing, removing, or retargeting host skills or plugins.
- Mutating Matt Pocock, Keystone, Thermos, Superpowers, Anthropic, or other externally owned source equipment.
- Treating a clean source review as plugin qualification, host convergence, live adoption, or release eligibility.
- Replacing Issue nisavid/provingkit#3's final refresh/qualification work or Issue nisavid/agents#51's convergence/removal work.

## Acceptance criteria

- The review is bound to the exact repository revision and exact source-evidence inputs.
- Every selected source is covered truthfully: material behaviors have one terminal migrate/drop decision, while a relevant source that yields no plugin contribution can be retained with its existing owner without inventing a destination.
- Tricritical's general-review baselines have complete behavior-level attribution and ablation evidence; no rule-level or verbatim preservation requirement remains.
- The evidence keeps source identity/license separate from semantic disposition and leaves managed upstream bytes unchanged.
- Receipt validation fails closed on missing, stale, substituted, mismatched, double-covered, orphaned, or unresolved final-release evidence.
- Tests cover the accepted source-only retain, behavior migration, and behavior drop shapes plus the receipt and path/provenance failure modes.
- Findings or a clean result are recorded without private machine paths, instruction contents, credentials, or secrets.
- Any remediation lands through separately reviewable changes and receives a fresh Daybreak review.

## Independent-review thread boundary

Begin the exact-candidate security pass in a fresh Daybreak thread independent of the implementation under review. If the pass finds changes to make, publish the findings and reviewed revision, invoke `handoff`, and move remediation to a separate fresh implementation thread. After the candidate changes, invoke `handoff` again to a different fresh Daybreak thread for exact-revision re-review. Follow [the coordinator's thread contract](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/41#thread-coordination). Suggested skills: `codex-security:security-diff-scan`, `codex-security:fix-finding`, `codex-security:verify-fix`, and `checkpointing-and-publishing-git-work`.

Before each review or mutation, coordinate candidate identity, evidence inputs, path ownership, and landing order with [Security-review source-skill lineage evidence with Daybreak Blue](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/5). Shared source-stage or validator inputs may have one active owner at a time; a changed shared input makes the sibling review and its handoff stale.

repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/8.title: Choose the production evidence producer and issuer boundary
repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/8.body:
## Question

What exact production producer, issuer, and candidate-binding contract can create and authenticate the Rolecasting execution evidence and independent Tricritical review, adjudication, and loop evidence that Task Witness and Mergecraft require for promotion, without treating checked-in fixtures or candidate self-attestation as live authority?

Settle:

- the producer and issuer identities, source and build ownership, trust roots, and independent review path;
- the exact immutable candidate, distribution, content-lock, host-route, execution, and evidence bindings;
- the provider, credential, secret, and local-versus-hosted execution boundaries;
- positive, unavailable, tamper, replay, substitution, partial-result, and recovery behavior;
- the two-host qualification and value-free evidence interface consumed by the Provingkit release contract; and
- the implementation, security-review, and promotion tickets that follow without weakening Task Witness or Mergecraft semantics.

This is a decision ticket. It authorizes planning and read-only inspection only. It does not authorize producer implementation, credential access, live inference, release promotion, publication, or host mutation. Resolve it with grilling, domain-modeling where the authority model is unclear, and the designated security route.

## Fresh-task boundary

Before resolution, create the native implementation, independent security-review, and host-qualification tickets required by the accepted decision. Then stop after publishing the durable answer and graph changes, invoke `handoff` to create a redacted continuation document under the operating-system temporary directory, and create one fresh orchestration task. That task may dispatch only independently unblocked work and must revalidate every ticket's authority before dispatch.

The handoff must name separate owners for production evidence-producer implementation; independent review/adjudication issuer implementation; Daybreak design and exact-artifact review with no implementation self-approval; and `hatchery` and work-mac qualification against the same immutable candidate, with each host task owning only its own evidence. It must also name the parallel Base Loadout controller and generic release-trust lanes, which may consume authenticated evidence but cannot define or mint it. No successor receives live inference, credential, promotion, publication, or host-mutation authority from this decision. Exact Codex task identifiers belong only in the redacted temporary handoff.

## Fresh entry boundary

Do not enter this decision as a continuation of [Audit the Provingkit promotion and release chain](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/2). The thread that resolves that audit must invoke `handoff` and start one fresh HITL thread for this issue after verifying that it is unassigned and unblocked. Follow [the coordinator's thread contract](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/41#thread-coordination). Suggested skills: `wayfinder`, `grilling`, `domain-modeling`, the designated security skill, and `handoff`.

Before discussion begins, the receiving thread must revalidate the live graph and coordinate its immutable inputs with any concurrent release-contract, source-security, Base Loadout, or generic release-trust threads. The existing post-resolution fresh-task boundary remains controlling for the implementation, independent-review, and host-qualification fan-out.

repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/8/commen.body:
## Design input: bounded review authority and the `Empiriarch` name

I am carrying `Empiriarch` into this decision as a provisional candidate name, not as accepted public Tricritical vocabulary.

The intended role is narrow: for one frozen candidate revision and its evidence, it selects the review focus, gives every finding a disposition, and returns the final clean or unclean judgment. It cannot author or mutate the candidate, request or perform revision, repeat the wider loop, mint or sign evidence, publish artifacts, or own the surrounding review system.

That boundary does not match one current Tricritical role. `review` selects reviewer scopes and synthesizes findings but does not adjudicate them; `adjudicate`, personified as Claimweigher, owns finding dispositions; and `loop`, personified as Fathomkeeper, sequences review, adjudication, optional revision, and terminal completion. The proposed authority therefore spans three current surfaces while intentionally excluding Fathomkeeper's repetition and mutation path. Renaming Claimweigher, the review coordinator, or Fathomkeeper would each misstate the authority.

I am not adding this to [the retained-guard port](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/38). That port preserves the current separation and leaves the production producer, issuer, admission, actuator, observer, and durable authorization decisions here.

This ticket should decide whether to:

1. preserve the current split and keep Claimweigher canonical; or
2. introduce a generic single-cycle review authority with this exact frozen-candidate, non-mutating boundary, then create an implementation successor that updates the topology, package vocabulary, validators, persona adapters, evals, and content identity together.

If the second option is accepted, `Empiriarch` remains only a candidate persona name. It must never name the signer, issuer, publisher, reviser, loop, or wider review system.

### Public-name disposition

`Empiriarch` is not cleared for public use. It is an exact term from *Torment: Tides of Numenera*, where the official [Traveler's Guide](https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/272270/manuals/Torment_Tides_of_Numenera_-_Traveler%27s_Guide_%28Manual%29.pdf) defines it as Sagus Cliffs slang for a headmaster or lead-reader. That gives it real semantic fit, but also makes it a direct franchise borrowing rather than a subtle allusion. Monte Cook Games' current [Fan Use Policy](https://www.montecookgames.com/fan-support/fan-use-policy/) does not clearly cover an unrelated public software role.

An exact-word search on 2026-09-04 found no live or dead USPTO result and no row in TMview, but that is only a preliminary screen. It did not complete WIPO or UK IPO searches, similar-mark and common-law searches, or class- and jurisdiction-specific clearance. WIPO's own [availability guidance](https://www.wipo.int/en/web/madrid-system/check-availability) warns that exact-name searching is insufficient. A pre-existing [GitHub account](https://github.com/Empiriarch) also creates an avoidable public namespace collision.

Until this ticket settles the authority shape and a dedicated naming-clearance step settles public suitability, keep the name provisional and internal. If the architecture accepts the new role, its implementation successor should either record completed clearance and any attribution conditions or choose an owned descriptive alternative before the persona enters public contracts, schemas, documentation, or UI.

This is a factual naming-risk screen, not legal advice.

repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/36.title: Integrate release-ops and publish the first signed Provingkit release
repos/nisavid/provingkit/issues/36.body:
## Outcome

Publish and independently accept the first authenticated Provingkit release through the operational release-ops system, then make that release available for Base Loadout adoption.

## Scope

- Release the cohesive seven-member Provingkit family selected by the existing release map.
- Keep GitHub Actions candidate-only: it may build, test, and attest, but it receives no production signing authority.
- Bind every member, manifest, dependency edge, promotion decision, and hosted artifact to the reviewed immutable source revisions.
- Authorize and sign on Hatchery, publish through GitHub Releases and canonical release state, and verify hosted readback.
- Independently verify the complete family and current status on `stlz-ivan-mbp`.

Host installation and Base Loadout activation remain in their existing adopter tickets.

## Acceptance evidence

- The release contract, promotion chain, issuer implementation, manifest, signatures, GitHub readback, canonical state, and independent verifier receipt agree on one artifact set.
- Candidate compromise cannot exercise release authority.
- The accepted release coordinates and immutable digests are ready for Base Loadout publication and dotfiles adoption.

## Execution

AFK preparation followed by operator-present authorization and signing.

## Fresh release-execution boundary

Do not enter this issue from a prerequisite's working conversation. After every native blocker closes and before any signing or publication mutation, invoke `handoff` and create a fresh release-orchestration thread. Follow [the coordinator's thread contract](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/41#thread-coordination). Suggested skills: `wayfinder`, `handling-privileged-steps`, `checkpointing-and-publishing-git-work`, `publishing-reviewable-prs`, and `pr-review-orchestration`.

The receiving orchestrator must revalidate the reviewed candidate, contract, promotion evidence, issuer implementation, accepted release-ops identity, and operator authority. Keep AFK preparation, operator-authorized Hatchery signing and publication, and independent work-mac verification in distinct fresh threads. Give every receiving thread the same immutable candidate and artifact digests and the sibling branch or task context; any mismatch or candidate change stops every affected thread. A handoff transfers context, never credentials, signing authority, publication authority, or host-mutation authority.

After independent acceptance, invoke `handoff` again before continuing into Base Loadout or portfolio-adoption work. The receiving coordinator must requery the graph and dispatch only successors that are independently unblocked, unassigned, and authorized.

repos/nisavid/agents/issues/41.title: Map the Provingkit release and Base Loadout adoption
repos/nisavid/agents/issues/41.body:
## Destination

Produce a decision-complete, evidence-bound route to publish one immutable Provingkit release, publish the portable Base Loadout that selects it, and materialize the exact resolved selection through dotfiles-owned Host Binding Profiles on Ivan's work macOS `stlz-ivan-mbp` system and personal CachyOS `hatchery` system, with every selected live harness validated and rollback ownership settled.

## Notes

- This map is the cross-repository coordinator and remains planning-only. Owner-local implementation stays in the linked Provingkit, Base Loadout, Agentworks, dotfiles, qualification, and host-migration lanes.
- **Provingkit** is the seven-member coordinated Kit containing Rolecasting, Tricritical, Versionkeeping, Mergecraft, Artifact Customs, Task Witness, and Tidesmith. It serves both as Agent Equipment built around constraining vibes with verification and as a proving ground for architectures that may later become generic Agentworks equipment.
- A Provingkit release is an immutable whole-Kit compatibility claim over exact independently releasable member identities. Individual plugins remain independently equipable, but a partial selection is not Provingkit.
- The first Provingkit release is cohesive and self-contained. Provingkit owns Mergecraft authoring, feedback semantics and placement, and both required response actuators, including source correlation, source-specific idempotency, exact-write verification, ambiguity handling, and receipts. Agentworks Discussion Comment transport remains independent equipment, not a Provingkit runtime capability provider or release prerequisite. Any later promotion or migration requires independent use, conformance evidence, released identities, and an explicit migration decision.
- **Agent Plugins Specification v1.0.0** is the external plugin package standard used by applicable members; it is not the Kit's name. Task Witness remains a code-only distribution with its own native-host qualification and promotion chain. Hindsight remains a separate program.
- `nisavid/agents` owns my personal loadouts, tools, and experiments. The initial **Base Loadout** is its only Loadout. [Publish the Base Loadout declaration](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/82) owns that portable declaration.
- `nisavid/dotfiles` owns only host- and environment-specific bindings, protected service installation, materialization, and host evidence. [Deploy the Base Loadout through dotfiles](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/68) owns that downstream realization.
- **Agentworks** is the formal generic Agent Equipment project, with **the Works** as an unambiguous shorthand. [Adopt the Agentworks identity and domain architecture](https://github.com/nisavid/agent-armory/issues/216) owns its independent rename and vocabulary rollout.
- [Adopt the Agent Plugins v1 stack](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/pull/39) is the historical source-stage baseline for the members that now form Provingkit.
- [Extract Provingkit into its release repository](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/81) is complete. `nisavid/provingkit` is the canonical public repository, with cutover completion bound to published `main` commit [`559fe97207c9a04aec4020072798f670e19b8598`](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/commit/559fe97207c9a04aec4020072798f670e19b8598). The repository still has no tags or releases.
- [agents PR #69](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/pull/69) remains open and unmerged at frozen head `02e3c721bdbd922883948bb3af84c5bafd702984`; Provingkit preserves its filtered candidate at frozen evidence commit `8edaf590736621352262457752d087bad835555d`. [Provingkit #38](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/38) owns a fresh destination draft without accepting the behavior. [agents #99](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/99) owns retiring active duplicate source after the remaining ports land.
- New Provingkit plugin source belongs in `nisavid/provingkit`. Historical references and compatibility evidence may continue to name `nisavid/agents`; active package, marketplace, validator, and release routes may not.

## Thread coordination

The native issue graph controls thread concurrency. Keep one active thread per claimed issue. Dispatch a successor only when it is open, unassigned, unblocked, and not reserved for operator-present work; do not create waiting tasks for blocked work.

At every issue-specific thread boundary, invoke `handoff` and save the redacted continuation document in the operating-system temporary directory, never in a repository or worktree. Link the controlling map and issue, resolution comments, pull requests, immutable commits, and published evidence instead of copying their bodies or diffs. Include a `Suggested skills` section. Redact secrets, credentials, personal information, and private host data; exact Codex task identifiers belong only in the temporary handoff.

Every receiving thread must reread the live map, native blockers, assignments, current default-branch revision, and linked pull-request heads before mutation, then claim only its named issue. Concurrent threads in this graph coordinate through issue comments, assignments, and branch or pull-request links: exchange exact base and head revisions, shared immutable inputs, path ownership, landing order, and invalidation notices before editing overlapping surfaces. A changed shared input makes dependent review and handoff state stale. A handoff transfers context, never implementation, credential, signing, publication, or host-mutation authority.

## Decisions so far

- [Inventory source-skill lineage and drift](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/49): [PR nisavid/agents#54](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/pull/54) established reproducible source and contribution identity, immutable initial-host snapshots, and explicit unresolved mappings without asserting current host freshness or release eligibility.
- [Define the source-skill disposition and release-refresh contract](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/50): [PR nisavid/agents#57](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/pull/57) established terminal contribution dispositions, a 24-hour final refresh and rescout ceiling, and evidence invalidation when candidate bytes change. [The security and correction lane](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/6) must complete before that baseline can support release eligibility.
- [Inventory unpublished Provingkit implementation and qualification](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/64#issuecomment-5494671865): published agents `main` commit [`44ee979cdae1d47f2ef3fdc713eaa6f04adf9892`](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/commit/44ee979cdae1d47f2ef3fdc713eaa6f04adf9892) is the cutover baseline. PR #69 remains retained extraction input rather than accepted production behavior. Only the unique published Linux qualification and macOS host-probe source blocks were adopted; stale evidence is not current qualification.
- [Inventory Mergecraft feedback and GitHub comment-operation coverage](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/66#issuecomment-5495032432), [superseded in ownership and dependency disposition](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/66#issuecomment-5501663545): current acquisition covers inline threads, top-level pull-request conversation comments, and submitted-review bodies, but normalization loses per-comment and per-review identity and no general response actuator or source-to-result correlation exists. For the first release, both missing response actuators and their operation evidence are Provingkit-owned.
- [Define Mergecraft feedback response surfaces and GitHub operation ownership](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/67#issuecomment-5498314539), [superseded in first-release ownership and dependency topology](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/67#issuecomment-5501681228): inline comments, pull-request conversation comments, and submitted-review bodies are distinct typed sources with the accepted inline-versus-top-level placement. Provingkit owns both response actuators, source correlation, idempotency, exact-reread and ambiguity behavior, and receipts without an Agentworks runtime or release dependency.
- [Define Issue Ops discussion-comment transport and source correlation](https://github.com/nisavid/agent-armory/issues/213#issuecomment-5500132599): Agentworks defines independent generic repository-qualified Discussion Comment equipment with source-specific idempotency, exact provider-result reread, bounded unknown reconciliation, and protected and portable receipts. It is not a Provingkit first-release runtime input.
- [Extract Provingkit into its release repository](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/81#issuecomment-5533504364): [PR #11](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/pull/11) established the destination source and history; [PR #37](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/pull/37) bound the reviewed carrier to final published history and a frozen non-release evidence ref. No release resource or live installation was created.

## Current frontier

- Finish the source cutover first. [Provingkit #25](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/25) and [#38](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/38) are unassigned, unblocked, and ready for an agent: #25 ports agents PRs #96–#98, while #38 publishes the retained PR #69 candidate as a destination draft.
- [agents #99](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/99) waits for #25 and #38, then removes active Provingkit source and discovery routes from `nisavid/agents`. It blocks [the promotion-chain audit](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/2), restoring the cutover prerequisite before release-chain work continues.
- [Inventory the selected live harness surfaces](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/42), [research release and update routes](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/1), [the promotion-chain audit](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/2), and [the README rework](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/32) remain assigned to `nisavid`. Revalidate each claim before resuming; #2 now waits for agents #99.
- [The Tidesmith map](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/12) is a child of this coordinator and blocks [the Provingkit release contract](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/3), so the first-release roster cannot silently omit its unfinished work.
- [The portable GitHub Markdown implementation](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/9) is unassigned and unblocked. [Mergecraft feedback response routing](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/10) waits only for #9. Both implementations belong in Provingkit and have no Agentworks runtime or release dependency.
- [Choose the production evidence producer and issuer boundary](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/8) follows #2 and blocks both [the release contract](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/3) and [first-release publication](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/36). It decides the trusted Rolecasting execution-evidence producer and the independent Tricritical review/adjudication issuer; it does not implement them.
- [The README rework](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/32) now blocks first-release publication, matching its explicit pre-first-release boundary.
- [Implement Issue Ops discussion-comment transport and receipts](https://github.com/nisavid/agent-armory/issues/215) remains valid independent Agentworks equipment work. It is not on the Provingkit first-release frontier and does not block Mergecraft response routing or the Provingkit release.
- [Bind GitHub text ownership into Base Loadout adoption](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/228) remains owner-local and owns the correction ledger, corrected Base Loadout and Host Binding Profile handoff, and final cross-repository graph verification.
- [Support authenticated HTTPS publication](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/4), [review source-lineage security](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/5), and [review and bind disposition evidence](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/6) remain explicit source and security work.
- [Define Base Loadout and two-host binding composition](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/46), [define live adoption and rollback](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/47), [converge source skills](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/51), and [produce the cross-repository handoff](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/48) remain downstream in native dependency order.
- [Publish the Base Loadout declaration](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/82) waits for the Provingkit release contract, the portable/host composition decision, source-skill convergence, and first-release publication. It then feeds dotfiles-owned host materialization.

## Not yet specified

- The promotion-chain audit must connect [authenticated HTTPS publication](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/4) to the first-release chain or record why that executor work is not a release blocker; #4 is currently otherwise disconnected.
- Before #8 closes, it must create the native implementation, independent security-review, and separate host-qualification tickets required by its accepted producer/issuer decision. No current issue substitutes for the safe authenticated status observer, trusted model-route issuer and policy admission, mandatory every-transition actuator, durable atomic single-use authorization ledger, independent Daybreak review, or two-host qualification. Those tickets must not introduce an Agentworks runtime or release dependency.

## Out of scope

- Hindsight and unrelated personal tooling in `nisavid/agents`.
- Implementing the Agentworks rename or promoting speculative Provingkit mechanisms into Agentworks through this map.
- Installing, migrating, publishing, provisioning release resources, or otherwise mutating live harness state while this planning map is being resolved.
- Simulating unsupported harnesses or forcing a Cartesian product across platforms.

## Downstream admission interface (2026-08-24)

The downstream dotfiles route has identified and ticketed a missing ordinary-PR branch in its App-pinned repository-transition gate. This does not change the coordinated six-distribution release contract.

For every pull-request head, the `Owner-signed age admission` App context must be present. An exact trusted-base calculation proving an empty protected-path set succeeds without a receipt; a nonempty set requires the separate owner-signed repository-transition receipt; uncertainty fails closed. The App-pinned context and its provenance remain unchanged.

This is separate from the source-skill reconciliation and release receipts governed by this map and [the convergence contract](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/51). Those receipts must not be reused as per-PR admission receipts, and a repository-transition admission result must not establish release eligibility, installation, or migration authority.

The downstream implementation and operator lanes are [dotfiles #167](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/167) through [#170](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/170). The agents thread coordinates only the interface at [dotfiles #112](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/112), [#124](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/124), and [#125](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/125); it does not broaden their acceptance criteria.

## Public release boundary decision (2026-08-25)

This issue governs the first public release of the six Agent Plugins v1 distributions. It does not govern the first private release of the dotfiles global-equipment tracker and installer; that system remains the sibling task's responsibility.

The first public qualification covers both audited hosts: work macOS (`sltz-ivan-mbp`) and Linux `hatchery`. A qualification cell is one host plus one distinct harness/provider route. Support the Codex, Claude, Cursor, and Cursor Agent routes where the host supports them; Claude Desktop is unsupported on `hatchery` and remains a macOS-only route. Cursor and Cursor Agent are separate routes, not one combined case.

Each supported route must pass a thorough local end-to-end smoke suite that exercises every meaningfully distinct path through every capability of every distribution, using the active operator inference accounts on both hosts. Evidence must be secret-free and record the route, capability, fixture/case, result, and failure class without retaining credentials or sensitive model responses. GitHub Actions automation is a later-release project; it must first settle endpoints, fixtures, limits, retries, and evidence retention.

The current macOS marketplace route is temporary. It may support pre-release work, but it is not the reproducible public release source until a clean pinned installation source and procedure exist.

repos/nisavid/agents/issues/99.title: Retire Provingkit source and discovery routes from nisavid/agents
repos/nisavid/agents/issues/99.body:
## Outcome

Remove the active duplicate Provingkit source and discovery routes from `nisavid/agents` after the remaining post-baseline landings are safely present in `nisavid/provingkit`. Leave this repository responsible for Hindsight, the Base Loadout, personal tools, and unrelated experiments.

## Relationships
